intelligence.human_view: A teacher who only checks the one question the student got right is not checking the homework — she checks the whole page, and she rips it apart because that is how the student learns. "Rip it apart, it's okay" is permission to do the job properly: an un-scored return is an unchecked claim. And the maths he did out loud so nobody can soften it: beautiful work at 93% waste is still 93% waste. The praise and the verdict live in the same breath. 10x is not ten times the agents; it is the root removed, so the same agents bank ten times the minutes.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build a big Lego castle and your friend checks every single brick — is it in the right place, does it look beautiful, is it all it can be? That's the scorecard. And instead of building one room at a time, all your friends build all the rooms at once — the kitchen, the bedroom, the tower — all together. That's parallel. And if you're only finishing 7 out of 100 bricks, that's not good — you find out why, and fix it, so you finish ten times more.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's like checking the whole homework, dear, not just the one question they got right, dear — you rip it apart, dear, because that's how it gets better, dear. And instead of doing one job at a time, dear, everybody works at once, dear — one on the kitchen, one on the bedroom, one on the tower, dear, all together. And if only 7 out of 100 are getting done, dear, that's not good, dear — you find out why, dear, and you fix it, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: SCORECARD EVERY RETURN — RIP IT APART, ARCHITECTURALLY AND FOR TEN-STAR SERVICE — BEFORE IT COUNTS AS DELIVERED. AND SCORECARD THE WHOLE SYSTEM, NOT JUST ONE PAGE. 10X THE WORKFLOW: FIND THE ROOT, SOLVE IT, PUT SYSTEMS IN PLACE SO WE GET MORE DONE. PARALLEL, NOT ONE AT A TIME.
